name: Lip mask (overnight)
lead: An overnight lip mask is a thick, occlusive lip treatment left on during sleep, in the same family as lip balm and petroleum jelly, which form a barrier that slows moisture loss from the lips. [1][2] People use it to wake up with smoother, softer, less flaky lips, which makes lips look fuller and more even and gives lipstick or bare lips a better surface. Overnight balms are described as using thicker emollients such as lanolin for longer moisture retention [3]; Wikipedia notes that medical-grade lanolin can speed healing of chapped lips. [4]

The category is closely associated with Korean beauty. Laneige, a brand launched in September 1994 by Amorepacific of Seoul, relaunched in the United States in September 2017 through Sephora with its Lip Sleeping Mask as the exclusive debut product. [6] Grokipedia names the Laneige mask as an example of an overnight lip treatment. [3] Other brands sell similar night-time lip products, and the format overlaps with slugging, the practice of applying a thick petrolatum layer before bed. [2]

No clinical trials of products sold as lip masks were found. The nearest research concerns lip balms and barrier products in general, including a 2015 study summarised on Wikipedia in which 32 women aged 20 to 40 showed improved lip condition and hydration lasting about eight hours after a lip balm, and which was funded by Burt's Bees. [1]

paras: Overnight lip masks are thicker than daytime lip balms, typically built from occlusives such as petrolatum, lanolin or waxes, often with oils and added ingredients. Lip balm in general forms an occlusive layer that seals in moisture and protects lips from cold, dry, windy conditions; common ingredients include beeswax, carnauba and candelilla wax, lanolin, paraffin and petrolatum, and some products add flavours, fragrance or sunscreen. [1]

Grokipedia lists the usual formulation building blocks as waxes such as beeswax and carnauba, butters such as shea and cocoa, oils such as coconut, jojoba and castor, and occlusives such as petrolatum, with vitamin E often added as an antioxidant. It describes thicker emollients such as lanolin as the choice for products meant for use during sleep. [3]

Petroleum jelly acts as an occlusive that reduces transepidermal water loss and is used to treat chapped lips; slugging is described as a popular version of this use. [2] The lips lack oil glands, so people with dry lips often reach for occlusive products, and overnight use gives the barrier hours without eating, drinking or licking.

Dry, peeling lips look rough and can make lipstick catch and settle into flakes. Cheilitis simplex, the medical term for chapped lips, involves cracking, fissuring and peeling, usually of the lower lip, and Wikipedia notes that saliva from habitual licking makes it worse. [4] A barrier layer left in place overnight is intended to keep the surface hydrated while this settles, which is the basis for the smoother, plumper-looking lips users describe in the morning.

Wikipedia notes that most chapped lips respond to barrier products such as lip salve or petroleum jelly. [4] Lip masks sit within that category and are marketed on the added pitch of a dedicated evening ritual.

Lip care itself is old: Egyptians reportedly made a lip treatment from beeswax, olive oil and animal fat as early as 40 BC. Robert Chesebrough was refining petroleum jelly in the 1870s, ChapStick was created in the early 1880s by Charles Browne Fleet, Carmex followed in 1937, Bonne Bell launched the first flavoured balm in 1973 and Burt's Bees released a beeswax balm in 1991. [1][2] Eos introduced its spherical balm in 2011. [1]

Laneige was launched by Amorepacific in September 1994 with a skin care collection called UV Green; its name comes from the French la neige, snow, and its central concept is Advanced Water Science, centred on hydration. [6] The brand opened its first international stores in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 2002, was sold at Target from 2014 to 2015, and has been stocked by Sephora Canada since September 2015. [6]

In September 2017 Laneige relaunched in the United States with Sephora, debuting its Lip Sleeping Mask as the exclusive product. [6] A 2019 rebrand refocused the company on a moisturising skincare portfolio. [6] Amorepacific, which owns Laneige alongside Sulwhasoo, Innisfree and Etude, is South Korea's largest cosmetics company. [7] Korean beauty more broadly has spread worldwide through the Korean wave, and the sleeping-mask format is one of its exports. [8]

Users generally apply a layer to the lips at the end of a night routine and leave it on overnight, wiping it off in the morning. Some people exfoliate gently beforehand or follow with lip colour the next day. Because the product is occlusive, it is typically applied to clean lips so the layer seals in moisture rather than trapping debris.
The mask is also used as a general-purpose balm during the day by people who prefer a thicker texture.

Contact allergy to lip-product ingredients such as beeswax and propolis has been reported. [5] Wikipedia notes that lip cosmetics, chiefly lipsticks and lip balms, are the most common cause of allergic contact cheilitis, and that patch testing can identify the trigger. [4]

In 2015 the German consumer organisation Stiftung Warentest reported mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons in some Vaseline products and advised against mineral-oil-based products for lip care; the European Food Safety Authority regards such compounds as possibly carcinogenic. [1][2] Wikipedia's petroleum jelly article says purity grades vary and that the EU limits polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in cosmetics. [2]

Dermatologists quoted on Wikipedia say fragrances and flavours in some balms can irritate, and the idea that lip balm is addictive is debated; other explanations given include lip licking, mouth breathing and weather. [1] Persistent cracking, swelling or sores that do not settle are typically assessed by a clinician, as cheilitis has infectious, allergic and sun-related forms. [4]

No studies found. Research on lip balm and petrolatum barrier products in general includes the 2015 balm study described above [1] and a reported trial of a lanolin-based balm for lip dryness in chemotherapy patients. [3]

card.summary: Thick overnight occlusive for lips; standard moisturizing care with no appearance trials.
card.note: Ingredient allergies such as beeswax or propolis are documented.

quick.overview:
An overnight lip mask is a heavy, occlusive lip product worn while sleeping. It works like thick lip balm.

No studies of lip masks specifically were found.
quick.mechanism: Occlusive ingredients such as petrolatum and lanolin slow water loss from the lips.
quick.risks: Allergic reactions to ingredients like beeswax and propolis have been reported.

chain: Thick occlusive layer applied at bedtime
Slows water loss from the lips overnight
Softer, less chapped lip surface in the morning
angle.text: A lip mask is applied as a thick layer before bed so the lips stay sealed and moisturised for hours. The visible effect is a smoother, more hydrated lip surface the next morning.
